doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Where the imagination on stage comes from
summary: Reeves says band members become co-creators on stage, feeding off each other so the music differs nightly.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we’re filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive at the college, and I’m really thrilled to have Dianne Reeves with me this evening. And I have to try to find an adjective to describe your performance, but I just was thrilled with the amount of imagination that was going on on stage. Can you in any way tell me where that comes from?

Well I think it comes from having a group of — standing inside of a group of musicians that become co-creators on stage, where it’s a very intimate exchange that happens between everybody. Everybody kind of feeds off of one another and so it makes the music different from night to night on a certain level.
